title: Moments
unit: IAL Mechanics (M1) (unit inferred from file name)

questions.question: Beam AB of weight 24 N and length 6 m is suspended horizontally by two light vertical ropes attached at C and D, where AC = x m and CD = 2 m. The tension in the rope at C is double the tension in the rope at D. The beam is a uniform rod in equilibrium. Find (i) the tension in the rope attached at D, (ii) the value of x.
questions.answer: (i) T_D = 8 N  (ii) x = 7/3 m, about 2.33 m
steps: Vertically: T_C + T_D = 24
With T_C = 2T_D: 3T_D = 24, so T_D = 8 N and T_C = 16 N
Moments about A (weight acts at midpoint, 3 m from A): 16x + 8(x + 2) = 24 x 3

questions.question: Uniform rod AB of length 2a and mass M is held horizontally by two light vertical strings attached at C and D, where AC = 2a/5 and DB = 3a/5. A particle P is placed on the rod at B and the rod remains horizontal and in equilibrium. Find, in terms of M, the largest possible mass of P.
steps: CD = a, and the rod's weight Mg acts at its centre, a from A
Let P have mass p and let the tension at C be T_C
Moments about D: T_C x a = Mg(2a/5) - pg(3a/5)
So T_C = (2M - 3p)g/5, and a string can only be in tension: T_C >= 0
Hence p <= 2M/3, so the largest mass of P is 2M/3

questions.question: Given that the mass of P is 3M/5, find, in terms of M and g, the tension in the string attached to the rod at C.
steps: From (a): T_C = (2M - 3p)g/5
With p = 3M/5: 2M - 9M/5 = M/5

questions.question: Beam AB of mass m kg and length 2 m is suspended by two light vertical ropes at C and D, where AC = 0.6 m and DB = 0.2 m. A particle of mass pm kg is attached to the beam at A and the beam remains horizontal. The tension in the rope at C is four times the tension in the rope at D. Using the model of a uniform rod, find the exact value of p.
steps: Vertically: T_C + T_D = (m + pm)g = m(1 + p)g
With T_C = 4T_D: 5T_D = m(1 + p)g
Moments about A (rod weight mg at 1 m; C at 0.6 m; D at 1.8 m): 0.6T_C + 1.8T_D = mg
Substitute T_C = 4T_D: 4.2T_D = mg, so T_D = 5mg/21

questions.question: The particle of mass pm kg at A is removed and replaced by a particle of mass qm kg at A. The beam remains in equilibrium horizontally but is on the point of tilting. Using the model, find the exact value of q.
steps: On the point of tilting the tension in the rope at D is zero (T_D = 0)
Vertically: T_C = (1 + q)mg
Moments about D (C is 1.2 m from D; rod weight is 0.8 m from D; A is 1.8 m from D): 1.2T_C = 0.8mg + 1.8qmg

questions.question: State how you have used the modelling assumption that the beam is uniform.
questions.answer: The weight of the beam is taken to act at its midpoint, 1 m from A.
steps: A uniform rod has its centre of mass at its midpoint
So the beam's weight mg acts at 1 m from A
This gives the moment mg x 1 used in the moments equations of parts (a) and (b)

questions.question: A metal girder AB of weight W N and length 6 m rests horizontally on supports C and D, where AC = DB = 1 m. When a force of 900 N is applied vertically upwards at A, the girder is about to tilt about D. When a force of 1500 N is applied vertically upwards at B, it is about to tilt about C. The girder is a non-uniform rod with centre of mass x m from A. Find x.
steps: Tilting about D: reaction at C is zero. Moments about D (A is 5 m from D): 900 x 5 = W(5 - x)
Tilting about C: reaction at D is zero. Moments about C (B is 5 m from C): 1500 x 5 = W(x - 1)

questions.question: A bead of mass 0.2 kg is attached to the end P of a light rod PQ. The bead is threaded on a fixed vertical rough wire and the rod is inclined to the wire at angle alpha, with tan alpha = 4/3. The thrust in the rod is T N and the bead is a particle. Find the magnitude and direction of the friction force acting on the bead when T = 2.5.
steps: The thrust pushes the bead away from Q: vertical component 3T/5 upwards, horizontal component 4T/5 pressing on the wire
Vertically with friction F taken upwards: F + 3T/5 - 0.2g = 0
F = 0.46 N, positive, so friction acts vertically upwards

questions.question: The coefficient of friction between the bead and the wire is mu. Given that the greatest possible value of T is 6.125, find the value of mu.
steps: Normal reaction from the wire N = 4T/5 (horizontal)
Greatest T: bead about to move up, so friction acts down with magnitude mu(4T/5)
Vertically: 3T/5 = 0.2g + mu(4T/5), so T(3 - 4mu) = g

questions.question: Uniform rod AB of length 5 m and mass 5 kg rests horizontally on supports C and D, where AC = 1 m and DB = 2 m. A particle of mass 10 kg is placed at A and a particle of mass M kg is placed at B. The rod remains horizontal and in equilibrium. Find, in terms of M, the magnitude of the reaction on the rod at C.
steps: D is 3 m from A; C is 2 m from D; rod weight 5g is 0.5 m from D (on the A side); 10g is 3 m from D; Mg is 2 m from D
Moments about D: R_C x 2 = 5g x 0.5 + 10g x 3 - Mg x 2

questions.question: Find, in terms of M, the magnitude of the reaction on the rod at D.
steps: Vertically: R_C + R_D = (5 + 10 + M)g = (15 + M)g
Check: moments about C give 2R_D = 4Mg - 2.5g, which agrees

questions.question: Hence, or otherwise, find the range of possible values of M.
steps: Each support can only push up, so R_C >= 0 and R_D >= 0

questions.question: Diving board AB is a uniform wooden plank of length 4 m and mass 30 kg, held horizontally by supports at A and C, where AC = 0.6 m. The force on the plank at A acts vertically downwards and the force at C acts vertically upwards. A diver of mass 50 kg stands at end B and is modelled as a particle. The plank is in equilibrium. Find (i) the magnitude of the force acting on the plank at A, (ii) the magnitude of the force acting on the plank at C.
questions.answer: (i) 1060g/3 N, about 3463 N  (ii) 1300g/3 N, about 4247 N
steps: Moments about C: the downward force F_A acts 0.6 m from C; the plank weight 30g is 1.4 m from C; the diver 50g is 3.4 m from C
F_A = 1060g/3 N, about 3463 N with g = 9.8
Vertically: F_C = F_A + 30g + 50g = F_A + 80g

questions.question: The support at A will break if subjected to a force greater than 5000 N. Find, in kg, the greatest integer mass of a diver who can stand on the board at B without breaking the support at A.
steps: For a diver of mass m kg at B: 0.6F_A = 30g x 1.4 + mg x 3.4, so F_A = (42 + 3.4m)g/0.6
Greatest integer mass is 77 kg

questions.question: Explain how you have used the fact that the diver is modelled as a particle.
questions.answer: The diver's weight is taken to act at the single point B, the end of the board.
steps: A particle has its whole mass at one point
So the diver's weight 50g acts at B, 3.4 m from C
This gives the moment 50g x 3.4 used in part (a)

questions.question: A non-uniform rod AB of length 9 m and mass M kg rests horizontally on supports at C (AC = 2.5 m) and D (DB = 2 m). The force on the rod at D is twice the force on the rod at C. The centre of mass of the rod is d m from A. Find d.
steps: Vertically: R_C + R_D = Mg, and R_D = 2R_C
So R_C = Mg/3 and R_D = 2Mg/3
D is 4.5 m from C; the centre of mass is (d - 2.5) m from C
Moments about C: (2Mg/3)(4.5) = Mg(d - 2.5)

questions.question: Beam ADCB of length 5 m lies on a horizontal step with end A on the step and end B projecting over the edge of the step at D, where DB = 1.3 m. C is at CB = 0.5 m. A boy of mass 30 kg stands on the beam at C and the beam is on the point of tilting. The boy is a particle and the beam is a uniform rod. Find the mass of the beam.
steps: On the point of tilting about D, the reaction at A is zero
Boy at C is 1.3 - 0.5 = 0.8 m from D
Centre of the beam is 2.5 m from A, so 1.2 m from D (on the A side)
Moments about D: 30g x 0.8 = mg x 1.2

questions.question: A block of mass X kg is placed on the beam at A and is modelled as a particle. Find the smallest value of X that will enable the boy to stand on the beam at B without the beam tilting.
steps: Tilting about D: the reaction at A must be non-negative
Block at A is 3.7 m from D; beam weight 20g is 1.2 m from D on the A side; boy at B is 1.3 m from D
Moments about D: 3.7Xg + 20g x 1.2 >= 30g x 1.3

questions.question: State how you have used the modelling assumption that the block is a particle in your calculations.
questions.answer: The block's weight acts at the single point A, 3.7 m from D.
steps: A particle has its whole mass at one point
So the block's weight Xg acts at A
This gives the moment Xg x 3.7 used in part (b)

questions.question: A branch AB of length 1.5 m rests horizontally on supports at C (AC = 0.24 m) and D (DB = 0.36 m). A 150 N force applied upwards at B makes the branch on the point of tilting about C. A 225 N force applied downwards at B makes it on the point of tilting about D. The branch is a non-uniform rod of weight W N with centre of mass x m from C. Use the model to find (i) the value of W, (ii) the value of x.
steps: Tilting about C with 150 N up at B (B is 1.26 m from C): 150 x 1.26 = Wx, so Wx = 189
Tilting about D with 225 N down at B (B is 0.36 m from D; C is 0.9 m from D): W(0.9 - x) = 225 x 0.36 = 81

questions.question: Non-uniform beam AB of mass 60 kg and length 8a m rests horizontally on two vertical supports, at C where AC = a and at D where DB = 2a. The normal reaction at D is three times the normal reaction at C. Modelling the beam as a non-uniform rod with centre of mass x m from A, find an expression for x in terms of a.
steps: R_C + R_D = 60g and R_D = 3R_C, so R_C = 15g and R_D = 45g
D is 6a from A, so D is 5a from C; the centre of mass is (x - a) from C
Moments about C: 45g x 5a = 60g(x - a)

questions.question: A box of mass M kg is placed on the beam at E, where AE = 2a. The beam remains in equilibrium horizontally, and the normal reactions at C and D are now equal. Modelling the box as a particle, find the value of M.
steps: Equal reactions: R_C = R_D = R, with 2R = (60 + M)g
Moments about A (centre of mass at 19a/4, box at 2a, C at a, D at 6a): Ra + 6Ra = 60g(19a/4) + Mg(2a)
